Across the sequence, it identifies the seated man in blue on the right, about 1.2–2.5 m away and facing the camera wearer, as well as the nearby standing people located approximately 0.4–2.0 m away at the left and right margins. Frame 1 contains separate masks for the yellow-shirted person cropped at the left edge, around 0.6 m away; the black-shirted person cropped at the right edge, roughly 0.5 m away and within reach; and the seated man between them, about 2.5 m distant. The wearer then turns and backs away in Frame 5. Relative to RGB, these instance masks define the overlapping body outlines of the closely grouped standing people in Frames 3 and 4 much more sharply. The system also fails in every frame to identify the reachable foreground table or its bag, bottles, and cans, and in Frame 4 it incorrectly labels a pastry inside the case behind the seated man as a 'donut'.
pose: The pose output follows 2D upper-body and leg landmarks in yellow, together with hand landmarks in magenta, SOLELY on the seated man wearing blue, who is approximately 1.2–2.5 m away in front of the cooler and display case. It excludes every other person and object in the scene. As the wearer closes the distance from about 2.5 m to 1.2 m in Frames 3 and 4, the head keypoints angle downward toward the table. His arm landmarks follow his right hand, kept within his own reach, from beside his face while he drinks in Frame 1 to his right knee, where he holds the cup near the foreground table in Frames 3 and 4. Those frames also contain a magenta hand cluster on his left hand as it rests on his left thigh, roughly 1.2 m from the wearer. When the wearer retreats in Frame 5, his right hand rises to his face again. This skeletal overlay exposes precise joint angles, his seated hip-to-knee configuration, and the direction of his head despite dark sunglasses and shadows concealing his eyes and lap in RGB. The result has several weaknesses: in Frame 1, the torso and left arm are incomplete; in the motion-blurred Frame 2, skeleton detection fails entirely; and while he grips the cup, the magenta finger keypoints of his right hand are absent. It also does not detect the nearby standing people, around 0.4–2.0 m away at the left and right edges, whose heads or bodies are partly outside the image or turned away.
